claims.text: DRDO revenue ₹11,850 cr plus capital ₹17,250.25 cr equals ₹29,100.25 cr already inside the four demands. Pension ₹8,000 cr Public Account recovery is an accounting deduction.

claims.alternative: Double-counting allocations or confusing gross/net can manufacture apparent missing money.
claims.falsifier: Reconcile original line items, receipts and recovery notes against Finance/Appropriation Accounts.

claims.response: Ministry explains long-term contracts, amendment difficulties and 352 IOPs created.

claims.falsifier: Treasury receipt and appeal/waiver ledger matching each penalty order would confirm or disprove non-recovery.

cases.title: AgustaWestland: trace contracts without converting allegations into convictions
cases.question: Which award, offset, reported payment, alleged intermediary and guarantee stages can actually be joined—and which later outcomes contradict an old narrative?
cases.period: 2011–2026 inquiry and litigation; 2006–2010 award context explicitly outside window
cases.finding: Named corporate links can be reconstructed from audit and court records, but alleged €6.05 m service payments are not trial-proven; a €18.2 m order is not proof of payment. Later acquittals and bail outcomes materially qualify earlier reporting.

geography.label: New Delhi
geography.basis: Administrative or audited-facility association, not a payment route, deployment coordinate or incident location.

geography.label: Mohali
geography.basis: Administrative or audited-facility association, not a payment route, deployment coordinate or incident location.

claims.text: CAG gives €556,262,026 prime contract and €166,879,000 offset obligation; the latter is not an additional payment to Government.
claims.response: Ministry 2013 defended compliance and described cancellation/recovery clauses.
claims.alternative: Scope, discounts, exchange rate and different financial stages can explain differing ₹3,600/₹3,726.96 crore headlines.
claims.falsifier: Use signed contract, invoice and currency-specific disbursement ledger.

claims.text: Prosecution allegations recited in March 2025 bail judgment attribute €6.05 m payments under a service agreement between AgustaWestland Holdings and Global Services FZE.
claims.response: Michel’s counsel denies specific role/material link; court granted bail on custody/trial-delay grounds, not on a final finding about the transfers.
claims.alternative: A lawful service fee or mischaracterised/duplicated record remains a rival explanation until bank trail, work product and applicable pact are proved.
claims.falsifier: Matched bank records plus contemporaneous legitimate deliverables or trial rejection would challenge the alleged sham-service mechanism.

claims.text: The same judgment recites a €18.2 m WG-30 buyback order to Global Trade & Commerce and investigators’ assertion of no dealings with Pawan Hans.
claims.response: The defence disputes material connection; no Pawan Hans sale/payment is admitted to this graph.
claims.alternative: Unperformed/cancelled order, documentary error or genuine intermediary correspondence could alter the allegation.
claims.falsifier: Pawan Hans contract, delivery and communication records would test whether a genuine transaction occurred.
missingRecords: Purchase order, amendment, cancellation and remittance records

claims.text: CAG found pre-contract IDS Infotech work included in a future offset programme, and an inadmissible civil-infrastructure component via Taneja.
claims.response: Ministry said only post-effective-date credit would be admissible and pointed to proposed amendments; vendor sought IDS deletion.
claims.alternative: Drafting/eligibility error later corrected can explain the problem without payment diversion.
claims.falsifier: Final amendment and accepted-credit certificates would show whether any ineligible credit actually survived.

claims.text: Leonardo 2019 filing reports former executives’ Italian acquittal survived appeal; Reuters 2025 reports Haschke acquittal. Michel obtained 2025 bail, while April 2026 HC rejected a separate release/extradition challenge.
claims.response: Acquittals and defence denials are retained prominently; Indian and Italian proceedings are not merged.
claims.alternative: Different defendants, charges and jurisdictions can yield different procedural and merits outcomes.
claims.falsifier: Original appellate judgments and current Indian docket would resolve the exact scope and any later reversal.

claims.text: 2016 report gives ₹1,620 cr paid and ₹2,068 cr guarantee recovery. Company records distinguish enforcement permissions, protected delivered-aircraft amounts and unresolved balances.
claims.response: Company challenged guarantee calls; later filing records partial relaxation and unresolved overall lawsuit.
claims.alternative: FX movements, performance bonds and delivered-goods entitlements explain why encashment need not equal refund or net fiscal gain.
claims.falsifier: A matched multicurrency ledger and final settlement/award could establish residual loss, recovery or entitlement.

whatWeKnow: Prime, offset, reported cash, alleged intermediary and bank guarantee stages remain separate.
The court text supports Michel-firm identity but does not independently audit beneficial ownership.
Later acquittals prevent recycling 2016 Italian convictions as current truth.
whatWeDoNotKnow: Ultimate recipients of alleged service payments are not established by inspected ledgers.
No link from these payments to a named minister, party, judge or attack is established.
October 2026 case outcome remains unresolved; a listing is not a ruling.

cases.title: HAL land monetisation: a stopped transaction is not a realised loss
cases.question: Did reserve-setting expose public land to undervaluation, and what did the audit correction prevent?
cases.period: 2015 policy follow-up; audit through 2023 with 2025 updates
cases.finding: CAG says HAL cancelled the ₹52.30 cr reserve process after audit and proposed ₹97.80 cr. This supports a control failure and corrective action; it does not establish a completed sale, ₹45.50 cr theft or an identified favoured buyer.

geography.label: Bengaluru
geography.basis: Administrative or audited-facility association, not a payment route, deployment coordinate or incident location.

claims.text: CAG describes use of one IBBI registered valuer for 2.925 acres, low ₹52.30 crore reserve, cancellation and new ₹97.80 crore reserve; it calls for investigation to fix responsibility.
claims.response: The cancellation and revised reserve are concrete contrary evidence to a claim of completed low-price disposal.
claims.alternative: Valuation method, encumbrances, tenure, date differences or administrative error could explain part of the difference; none have been independently quantified.
claims.falsifier: Original valuation, comparable sales, board approval, cancellation and subsequent auction outcomes can establish whether like-for-like underpricing existed and whether any sale occurred.

whatWeKnow: Auditor reports risk and a corrective reversal.
Valuer and prospective buyer are not named in inspected brief.
whatWeDoNotKnow: No completed disposal, payment, beneficiary, politician relationship or disciplinary outcome is established.

nextRecords.record: Original / revised valuation with encumbrance schedule
Board approval, cancellation and sale / auction record
nextRecords.purpose: Establish transaction stop and any later receipt

limits: Official summary only; full audit working papers still needed.
Do not treat ₹45.50 cr difference as money lost, recovered or paid.

actors.authority: PSU responsible for its land management and monetisation, as audited.
actors.incentive: Analytical possibility: unlock land value efficiently while complying with valuation and approval controls.

actors.authority: Audits HAL land management and calls for responsibility investigation.
actors.incentive: Analytical possibility: prevent undervalue and strengthen public asset controls.

informationThen: Exact original decision date and valuation inputs unknown; no reconstructed claim that actors knew 2025 audit findings.

options.label: Proceed subject to substantiated valuation and competitive process
options.expectedObservableOutcome: Independent valuation review, reasoned approval, bid results and registered deed.

options.label: Cancel and revalue before proceeding
options.expectedObservableOutcome: Cancellation record, new reserve and later auction document.

decisionAnalysis.observedOutcome: CAG reports cancellation and revised reserve; completed new auction outcome unknown.
hindsightLimits: Options are institutional analytical alternatives, not mind reading.
No causal claim that ₹45.50 crore was saved; reserve differences are not realised values.

cases.title: Defence corporatisation meets public healthcare
cases.question: Who owns hospital obligations after ordnance corporatisation, and do expenditure and service measures match the new responsibilities?
cases.finding: CAG reports ₹598.84 crore spent on Ordnance Factory Hospitals in 2020–24 and staffing/utilisation/regulatory gaps in eight selected hospitals. Hospital transfer and health-service merger decisions remained pending in the cited 2025 record.

geography.label: New Delhi
geography.basis: Administrative or audited-facility association, not a payment route, deployment coordinate or incident location.

claims.text: The official brief reports ₹598.84 crore network spending, more than 82% on pay; audit of eight selected hospitals found staffing / service mismatch, limited specialist/diagnostic services and post-corporatisation framework gaps.
claims.response: MoD June 2025: new DPSUs should focus on production, no legal obligation to operate hospitals, transfer under consideration.
claims.alternative: Primary-care, same-day treatment, remote access and standby capacity can explain low inpatient occupancy; payroll share alone is not waste or fraud.
claims.falsifier: Facility-level beneficiary load, referral costs, service mix and staffing standards could establish whether costly duplication or essential access predominates.

whatWeKnow: Cabinet 2021 corporatisation created seven DPSUs; management of OFHs placed under DoO(C&S), DDP.
Audit record provides a real defence-health-administration join, not a private payment recipient.
whatWeDoNotKnow: No private hospital vendor, diverted payment or outcome of pending 2025 decisions is established.
The all-India healthcare implications cannot be inferred from this selected sample.
